messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: P1 - elevated error rate and latency on inference gateway - affected routes: /v1/generate (region-us-west). Auto-escalation to #incidents.
Sam (oncall): I’m on it, pulling traces now. Any customer-facing alerts?
Support-Bot: Customer-facing errors: 11 complaints in the last 10m, 3 high-traffic tenants showing >500ms tail latency and occasional 503s.
Nisha: saw a sudden drop in prefix cache hitrate on the dashboard at 14:03 UTC, deltas in prefix-kv hit% from ~92% -> ~55% across many nodes.
Sam (oncall): ok timeline note: hitdrop starts ~14:02-14:04 UTC. Can infra share logs for cache invalidations?
Maria (infra): collecting /var/log/redwood/cache/*.log + shard metrics. Uploading aggregated logs to s3://redwood-incident-logs/2123456789/cache-aggregate.log (will paste tail).
Maria (infra): tail of cache log:
```
[14:03:07] shard-12 INFO prefix_cache: eviction policy triggered, evicted 128 entries, reclaim 1.2MB
[14:03:08] shard-12 WARN prefix_cache: unexpected TTL-sync gap for namespace default, delta=6s
[14:03:09] shard-09 INFO kv_cache: reuse=false for request batch 0x7f3a
[14:03:10] shard-15 WARN prefix_cache: mass-invalidate called by rollout-controller for model-id=m-3b-quant
[14:03:11] shard-01 INFO prefix_cache: hit_rate=0.57, warmup_inflight=412
```
Sam (oncall): mass-invalidate by rollout-controller at 14:03 — that stands out. Was there a deployment/rollout?
Jordan (eng-ml): I just saw a partial canary for m-3b-quant earlier but it finished at 13:50. No scheduled invalidation at 14:03 in the rollout config. Checking rollout logs.
Jordan (eng-ml): rollout-controller logs show a spike of delete_prefix for model-id=m-3b-quant at 14:03 triggered by `auto-refresh` path due to stale manifest checksum mismatch. It cascaded to a full prefix purge on many shards.
Nisha: so hypothesis 1: manifest drift triggered automated prefix invalidation -> mass cache misses -> KV reuse disabled -> tail latency and 503s.
Infra-SRE: hypothesis 2: simultaneous eviction storm combined with TTL-sync gap caused rewarm to overload backend and blocked reuse. We need to distinguish.
Sam (oncall): both are plausible. Let's build a minimal timeline and tag evidence snippets.
Sam (oncall): TIMELINE (UTC):
- 14:00 - 14:02: baseline hit_rate ~92%
- 14:03:07: rollout-controller issues mass-invalidate for m-3b-quant
- 14:03:09: logs show kv_cache reuse=false for many batches
- 14:03:10 - 14:10: clients experience elevated latency and 503s; support tickets appear
- 14:08:00: temporary mitigation: disabled auto-refresh and re-enabled soft-reuse flag on shard groups
- 14:12:00: hit_rate starts recovering, back to ~85% by 14:20
Sam (oncall): evidence: attached log chunk + dashboard snapshot (see s3 link above).
Maria (infra): sharing node-level metric excerpt: request_rate per shard spiked x3, rewarm_inflight peaked at 9x normal, eviction_count spiked. Uploading CSV to s3://redwood-incident-logs/2123456789/shard-metrics.csv
Nisha: important: the invalidation targeted prefixes for m-3b-quant but we see other unrelated model prefixes also drop. Could rollout-controller have used a wildcard erroneously?
Jordan (eng-ml): looking through the invalidation payloads — the manifest key parsing had a regex that matched `m-3b` and `m-3b-quant` but due to a missing anchor it expanded to `m-3b*` which hit `m-3b-v2` etc. Basically over-broad invalidation.
Infra-SRE: that explains unrelated model prefix misses. Root cause likely a rollout-controller regex bug + an opportunistic eviction storm + TTL-sync gap.
Sam (oncall): mitigation steps taken in-thread: 1) rolled back invalidation command via controller (disabled auto-refresh) 2) toggled kv_cache soft-reuse=true to allow cache reuse for in-flight requests 3) manually seeded hot prefixes for top tenants (partial warmup). Did we also throttle rewarm throughput?
Maria (infra): yes we applied temporary per-shard rewarm throttle at 14:08 to keep backend steady: `echo 200 > /proc/sys/redwood/rewarm_max_qps` on affected nodes.
Support-Bot: Current customer impact summary: 3 tenants impacted, average additional cost ~2.3x due to fallback model usage for 24m window. No data exfiltration or auth failures.
Sam (oncall): request: Jordan/Nisha please verify whether the soft-reuse flip has any correctness implications for model outputs. We need to be sure quality unchanged.
Jordan (eng-ml): soft-reuse only allows KV cache reuse for token prefixes where the model variant is compatible. No mixing across quantized/different-arch models. Quick unit check passes on sample prompts. :white_check_mark:
Nisha: action items draft in-thread:
- infra: root cause assemble (regex bug in rollout-controller + TTL-sync timing) [Maria, Infra-SRE]
- eng-ml: validate soft-reuse correctness and prepare revert plan if issues found [Jordan]
- devex: update rollout-controller manifest parsing tests and add anchor checks [Sam/Jordan]
- ops: add guardrails to prevent mass-invalidate without dry-run and an approval gate for >N prefixes [Maria]
- support: notify affected tenants with incident summary and cost mitigation options [Support-Bot]
Sam (oncall): assigning on-call followup: Maria take infra RCA lead; Jordan take model-safety signoff; Nisha will assemble timeline and hit-rate graphs for postmortem.
Maria (infra): starting RCA doc at https://redwood.internal/rca/2123456789 (draft) — will paste key logs there.
Infra-SRE: note for postmortem: correlate TTL-sync gap windows with NTP skew across host OS images; saw similar TTL drift in canary last month.
Sam (oncall): immediate post-incident mitigation checklist complete? Anyone seeing residual error spikes?
Nisha: spikes at low-levels remain on shard-09 but not customer-facing. Monitoring alerting to follow; schedule follow-up 1:1 with rollout-controller owners.
Support-Bot: created incident ticket INC-2123456789 and emailed affected tenants with credits offer template.
Sam (oncall): final note: Hypothesis pinned in thread: primary cause = rollout-controller regex bug causing mass prefix invalidation; contributing factors = eviction storm + TTL-sync gap that slowed rewarm and prevented quick reuse. We’ll capture evidence in the RCA doc. Thanks all — handing to Maria for the document and assignees. :handshake:
